summary: PalDat records mature pollen shape and dispersal unit (monad or otherwise) per taxon, which covers the outcome side of the claim, but no repository record links this to when the wall hardens relative to tetrad separation; BioImage Archive has no tetrad-development series (9 'pollen tetrad' hits, all about tubes or nuclei) and Dryad's closest set concerns conifer malformations.
next_step: Take shape and unit type from PalDat for taxa with permanent tetrads versus monads, and compile wall-timing evidence (callose and exine formation stages) from developmental papers for the same taxa; mature morphology alone cannot supply the mechanism.
obstacles_confirmed: PalDat records shape and whether grains are united, not the developmental timing of wall hardening relative to separation.
Mature shape alone cannot establish wall-hardening time.
